messages:
Sam: Quick heads-up — Atlas just announced 'FastRoute' which looks a lot like tenant-level routing. ACME (pilot customer) asked whether we can match this by EoQ. We need to decide parity vs a differentiated path. Low churn risk but tight eng bandwidth. Thoughts?
Jamie: Do we have the announcement link? And ACME's deadline exactly?
Sam: Link: https://paper.internal/atlas-fastroute (copy pasted). ACME wants a pilot ready by EOW of next quarter. They're explicit about simple setup + SLA.
Maria: ACME is the highest-risk pilot right now; losing them is ~120k ARR and a lot of referral value. Their ask: per-tenant routing + admin UI + SLA. They said simpler setup could tempt them to switch.
Alex: From infra side, parity means two major pieces: 1) policy engine for per-tenant routing (~3wks dev + testing) and 2) admin UI (~2wks). Main risk is rollout/backwards compatibility with existing route cache + KV. We could split policy engine first.
Tyler: Engineering suggestion: implement a lightweight config-driven fallback routing and feature-flag the full policy engine. Rough estimate: policy engine MVP 2.5wks (small focused pair) + 1wk QA. UI can be lower priority.
Diane: Design: can produce a proto admin panel that reuses our current route templates. Minimal screens: list, create policy, attach to tenant. Should be able to mock in 1 sprint.
Jamie: Sales/positioning tradeoff — parity is defensive (keeps ACME), differentiator could be 'routing + built-in telemetry/observability' which ACME also mentioned as high value. Can we scope to "parity+" (minimal parity + telemetry hooks)?
Sam: Proposal checklist:
```
- MVP policy engine (per-tenant routing) [owner: Alex]
- Admin proto UI (CRUD for policies) [owner: Diane/Jamie]
- Telemetry hooks (token-level routing tags, trace/span enrichment) [owner: Tyler]
- Canary plan: 10% traffic -> ACME -> monitor latency & error rate
- Launch criteria: p95 regression <= 25ms, error rate < 0.1%, telemetry ingest cost bump <= 10%
```
Alex: Sounds reasonable. Notes: will need feature-flagging + rollout plan. Also recommend a quantization profile parameter to mitigate latency regression for heavy models when routing changes.
Tyler: I'll spike the feature-flagging and fallback behavior today. If we prioritize policy engine first, we can aim for MVP across 3 sprints.
Maria: I'll confirm ACME's willingness to be a canary customer and whether they'd accept pilot pricing. That gives us room to iterate post-canny.
Sam: Decision for now: ship parity-MVP with telemetry hooks (parity+). Policy engine first, UI in parallel, canary with ACME. I'll create the roadmap ticket and flag dependencies. @deploy-bot please create a tracking JIRA and link it here.
deploy-bot: Created JIRA PR-987 "tenant-routing MVP (parity+)" and Trello card. Links: https://jira.internal/PR-987 https://trello.com/c/tenant-routing
Jamie: :thumbsup: I'll update the product spec doc and schedule a 30min sync with design + eng tomorrow to finalize owners and milestone dates.
